document.title: Terrorism Finance: Updating the Taliban Names Designated Under UNSCR 1267 (State 098588)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban Biography: The Structure and Leadership of the Taliban 1996-2002
document.note: [Secret] Update giving names and positions of 75 Taliban officials, compiled to support UNSCR 1267 asset freezes. Describes Mullah Amir Khan Muttaqi as a key figure in the Taliban's ideological projects who led a 1997 UNOCAL-invited delegation to the U.S. Excised.

key_claims: The US compiled an updated Taliban list based on information from Nov 2001 onward to replace the 152 Taliban names on the UN 1267 list.
Mullah Omar reportedly married a daughter of Usama bin Ladin, linking Taliban and al-Qa'ida leadership.
Jalaluddin Haqqani, a Zadran from Khost, was a strongman of the southeastern zone, joined Hezb-i-Islami (Khalis) in 1979 and solicited Arab donations.
Maulawi Abdul Kabir, a former Haqqani commander and teacher, controlled eastern-zone smuggling routes and allegedly laundered large sums.
Turabi controlled key monetary decisions; Mohtasim controlled the flow of money as Rais Hayat Khas.
Darul Uloom Haqqania at Akora Khattak educated several senior Taliban (Haqqani, Kabir, Rahmani).
Many senior Taliban were affiliated with Hezb-i-Islami (Khalis), Harakat-i-Inqilab or Ittehad-i-Islami during the anti-Soviet jihad.
Taliban control was limited in the Paktia-Khost-Paktika region, where tribal leaders and commanders mattered more.
The US sought to update the UNSCR 1267 Taliban designations with a roster of Taliban provincial governors, corps commanders and aides.
Rahmani, the Kandahar governor, studied at Darul Uloom Haqqania (Akora Khattak) and Farooqia in Karachi before joining the Taliban in 1994.
Several Taliban northern commanders (Daidullah, Fazel, Razaq, Qahir) were tied to Mazar-e-Sharif; Daidullah is blamed for abuses there in August 1998 and for burning Yakawlong in June 2001.
Rocketi had earlier fought alongside Sayyaf's Ittehad-i-Islami and joined the Taliban in fall 1994.
The Taliban had little control over Paktia, Khost and Paktika, where tribal leaders and senior commanders mattered more.
Mullah Omar's aides Haji Lala and Tayeb Agha, and diplomats such as Mujahid and Waziri, were also listed.
